title: Reduce prefill-side tokenizer overhead with hot-lane lexer and prioritized prewarm
creator: Alicia Chen
description: This ticket targets reducing prefill-side CPU and latency overhead for short-to-medium prompts by introducing a specialized hot-lane lexer + prioritized prewarm. The goal is to remove repetitive parsing work, reduce OS scheduling jitter from many small prefill tasks, and integrate a prefill-aware kernel selection hint into the runtime so that decode scheduling can favor warmed KV caches.
acceptance_criteria: Tokenization throughput for 16-256 token prompts increases by >= 1.8x in the hot-lane case compared to baseline.
Median prefill CPU time per request drops by >= 40% on p3-like instance profiles for real workload mix.
No regressions for long prompts (>2048 tokens).
Integration: runtime can consume a prefill-ready token buffer and apply kernel-selection hint without additional allocations.
Unit + perf tests added to CI; benchmark dashboard updated with reproducible harness and seed prompts.
steps_taken: 2026-02-26: Spike implemented a fast-path lexer that fuses whitespace and ASCII scanning using SIMD-friendly loops (Alicia).
2026-03-01: Microbenchmark harness created; ran 10k samples from prod-like prompt corpus to measure hot-lane candidate hit rate.
2026-03-02: Implemented per-customer prefix cache keyed by 64-bit prompt hash with small LRU; stress-tested for memory churn (Priya).
2026-03-03: Added runtime hint API: prefill_hotlane=true plus expected_max_tokens to allow kernel selection for small sequence lengths (Marco).
2026-03-04: Initial end-to-end benchmark: integrated hot-lane lexer + prewarm; observed decreased tail latency but some contention on allocator paths.
benchmarks: Baseline median prefill CPU: 8.1ms (on 8 vCPU p3-equivalent worker)
Subtotal end-to-end latency improvement for 32-token prompts: 12% median, 25% p95
Memory overhead for per-customer prefix cache: 8MB per 10k active customers under current TTL settings
blockers: Allocator contention observed under high concurrency: need to swap to arena allocator for small buffers (ENG-51299).
Decision on shard key for customer prefix cache TTL vs LRU behavior pending (security and memory trade-offs).
Cross-team alignment required with Kernel Selection (ENG-51900) to make runtime hints non-breaking.
decisions: Opted for a separate hot-lane lexer code-path that is explicitly invoked by prefill-stage when prompt length < 300 tokens and contains only ASCII/UTF-8 normal chars.
Prefix cache uses 64-bit XXHash of normalized prompt with optional tenant salt; cache entries are small packed token buffers to avoid reallocation.
Kernel-selection hint is an advisory boolean + expected_max_tokens integer; runtime may ignore if incompatible with target hardware.
next_steps: Replace small buffer allocator with per-thread arena and rerun high-concurrency benchmarks (owner: Daniel Kim).
Finalize cache eviction policy: TTL 60s + LRU for hot customers; measure false-positive retention impact on memory (owner: Priya Patel).
Work with Kernel Selection team to expose hint surface in SDK and validate non-breaking behavior on A100 and T4 clusters (owner: Marco).
Add synthetic adversarial prompts to perf suite to ensure no correctness regressions in tokenization.
notes: Avoid inlining complex Unicode normalization in hot-path; we defer to slow path for non-ASCII to keep hot lane deterministic and fast.
We intentionally keep hot-lane heuristic conservative to prevent silent correctness bugs for edge-case tokens (emoji, ZWJ sequences).
If allocator fix is non-trivial, consider feature flagging hot-lane behind runtime config and gradual rollout via Canary in Console.
